 Mavericks-Timberwolves preview: Measuring-stick trip starts in Minnesota
 Dwain Price November 12, 2026 12:22 PM CST Starting with Thursday’s game against the Minnesota Timberwolves, the Dallas Mavericks are about to face one of their most consequential road trips of the season. 
 Not only will the Mavs face the 8-3 Timberwolves. But they’re also playing the Cavaliers in Cleveland (6-6) on Saturday and will end the trip in Boston on Sunday against the 10-2 Celtics.
 The Timberwolves are fifth in the Western Conference and are the only team to win in Houston (117-107) this season. Meanwhile, the Cavaliers defeated Minnesota, 127-125, in overtime on Oct. 26, and also own victories over the highly-touted Philadelphia 76ers (119-95) and defending world champion New York Knicks (115-107).
 The Celtics have the best record in the Eastern Conference and are tied with San Antonio for the second-best record in the NBA and just spanked the Sixers in Philadelphia on Tuesday, 123-101.
 So the three road games in four days will give the Mavs (7-4) somewhat of a measuring stick of where they are at this point of the young season.
 “It’s a great test for us,” Mavs forward P.J. Washington said. “I think everybody is excited obviously to play some good teams. “It’s some good matchups, so it’s definitely going to be a great trip for us.”
 Although the Timberwolves are without four-time All-Star guard Anthony Edwards – he underwent a right knee arthroscopic debridement procedure on Oct. 29 – they’ve still been able to forge ahead.
 “Minnesota is very good,” Mavs coach Dusty May said. “They have guys that can space the floor, they’ve got very individual defenders, they’ve got tough, tough shot-makers (and) they present a number of challenges.
 “We’re going to see where we are. We’ve got to be able to go on the road and play a really good sound basketball game. We’ve proven that we can do that. Obviously, not against Minnesota, but we've proven we can play well away from our arena.”
 The Mavs are 2-2 on the road this season with the wins coming in Indiana (121-105) and in Miami (113-109). But they’re facing a different set of challenges on Thursday in Minnesota point guard LaMelo Ball (18.3 ppg, 6.0 apg) and shooting guard Ayo Dosunmu (18.1 ppg).
 Couple that with what the T-Wolves get from Jaden McDaniels (17 ppg, 6.1 rpg), Jonathan Kuminga (12.3 ppg, 5.5 rpg) and Rudy Gobert (7.8 ppg, 12.1 rpg), and the Mavs will likely have their hands full trying to keep up with the defensive-minded Timberwolves.
 “He’s special,” May said in reference to Ball. “His ability to score off the bounce, he can give his teammates wide open shots, he creates offense single-handedly and he’s fun to watch.
  “He’s entertaining. He’s got great energy and you can tell he loves to hoop.”
 May is impressed with the way Minnesota has gone about its business sans Edwards, who has only played four games this season.
 “Ayo has been pressed into a bigger role and he’s showed that he’s more than prepared for it,” May said. “Bones Hyland has played well. You can go down the list.
 “LaMelo and Jaden, they’ve gotten a few more touches and a few more shots. I don’t want to say they’re just as good, but they’re really good obviously when they lead with Ant, and they’re really, really good without him.”
 Here’s what else to look for: 
 *The Mavs didn’t win their seventh game last season until Dec. 1 with a 131-121 victory in Denver. At that point the Mavs were 7-15. Now, the Mavs are 7-4 and forward Washington said: “It feels great. Everybody’s smiling, everybody’s excited. There’s a lot of joy in the city right now, obviously. So, for us the big thing is just to keep pushing one game at a time and just try to stack up wins.”
 *Minnesota is 4-1 at home this season with its lone home loss coming on Oct. 28 against the Golden State Warriors (119-118). It was the Timberwolves’ first game after Anthony Edwards suffered his right knee injury.
 *Washington would like to see the Mavs make some improvements on the defensive end of the floor. “Defensive rebounding is an area we need to improve,” he said. “I feel like defensively when we pressure teams I feel like our defense is one of the best in the league. But when we don’t pressure teams, that leaves to us being lackadaisical and teams scoring easy. So, for us I think it’s pressuring teams and trying to set a tone on that end.”
 *The Timberwolves advanced to the Western Conference Finals in 2024 and 2025, but were eliminated in the conference semifinals last season by the San Antonio Spurs in six games. The major offseason changes Minnesota made this summer were bringing in point guard Ball and Kuminga. Julius Randle was the key loss.
 Dallas Mavericks (7-4) at Minnesota Timberwolves (8-3)     
 WHEN : Thursday, 7 p.m.    
 WHERE : Target Center, Minneapolis 
 TV : KFAA-29, MavsTV+, NBA TV 
 RADIO : 105.3 The Fan, 99.1 FM Zona MX (Spanish)
